sentences: Mesh (9,282), geometry (195) and compute (2,689) now translate; `s_swappc_b64` is replaced by Vulkan vertex inputs (see *Vertex fetch*) and the `tbuffer_load_format_*` forms use the instruction's format.
Packed `tbuffer_load_format_d16_{x,xy,xyz,xyzw}` load two 16-bit components per VGPR, with the same final partial write as MUBUF.
Native gfx1036 wave32/64 confirmed all four widths for RGBA8_UINT and RGBA8_UNORM with a conflicting 32_UINT V# format.
Both packed and ordinary MTBUF loads ignore the V# channel selectors and use identity for the instruction format, zero-filling missing channels.
Native gfx1036 measurements compared multiple V# permutations with MUBUF as a control.
An INVALID V# format (0) suppresses the MTBUF fetch even at a valid address inside its bounds.

Native gfx1036 wave32/64 returned zero components at all four widths and preserved the untouched half of an odd D16 destination, as specified for unbound resources in the [RDNA2 ISA, §8.1.4](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf).
A translated vertex fetch on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics also followed a change to the instruction format between two draws with identical vertex records and V#.

Fixed UNORM and SNORM loads share the exact integer quotient for each magnitude width across instructions and channels (checked against rationally rounded binary32 values on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics).
The gfx1013 disassembler omits `format:` for the [GFX10 MTBUF default](https://llvm.org/docs/AMDGPUModifierSyntax.html#ufmt), `BUF_FMT_8_UNORM` (code 1).
A few rare ops are still reported by name rather than guessed.
